title: Aligning Active Inference Ontology to SUMO
description: This document aims to act as a scaffolding, displaying a tentative alignment of Active Inference terms with SUMO entities, in order to facilitate the anticipated process of rigorously mapping Active Inference to the SUMO formal ontology.

methods.name: Tentative term-by-term alignment of Active Inference topics to SUMO entities
methods.description: Built an alignment table proposing, for a subset of Active Inference Ontology terms, the SUMO files, supersets, subsets and relations likely to correspond to each topic.

methods.name: Grouping Active Inference topics into modules and core/entailed/supplemental lists
methods.description: Organized topics into informal modules (e.g. Action, Bayesian Statistics, Markov Partitioning) and assigned each to one of three exposition lists.
methods.evidence: List. Each individual topics has been assigned to one of three “lists.” This is a porous partition, created to help organize exposition.

methods.name: Structured SUMO columns: superclass/instanceOf, subclasses, domains, other relations
methods.description: Situated each aligned term in SUMO via columns for more-general relations, less-general subclasses/subrelations, argument domains, and other SUMO relations.
methods.evidence: this column situates a conceptual entity in the whole SUMO ontology by showing the term’s place one or more “upward” or “including” or contextual or more-general relationships

methods.name: Flagging proposed terms absent from SUMO with an asterisk
methods.description: Marked candidate terms not yet present in SUMO with an asterisk prefix (e.g. *ActiveState), indicating where new SUMO topics would be needed.
methods.evidence: In this document, we often flag terms that do not yet belong to SUMO by prefixing an asterisk (as in “*ActiveState”).

key_findings: The document provides a scaffolding: a tentative alignment of Active Inference terms with SUMO entities, intended to support a later rigorous mapping of Active Inference to SUMO.
The alignment table shows, for many core Active Inference terms, SUMO areas likely to hold corresponding topics or where new topics should be created to better match Active Inference concepts.
